source_text: Isti igitur impuri spiritus, daemones, ut ostensum a magis, a philosophis, et a Platone, sub statuis et imaginibus consecrati delitescunt, et afflatu suo auctoritatem, quasi praesentis numinis, consequuntur, dum inspirantur interim vatibus, dum fanis immorantur, dum nonnumquam extorum fibras animant, avium volatus gubernant, sortes regunt, oracula efficiunt falsis pluribus involuta. Nam et falluntur et fallunt, ut et nescientes sinceram veritatem, et quam sciunt, in perditionem sui non confitentes. Sic a coelo deorsum gravant, et a Deo vero ad materias avocant, vitam turbant, omnes inquietant, irrepentes etiam corporibus occulte, ut spiritus tenues, morbos fingunt, terrent mentes, membra distorquent, ut ad cultum sui cogant: ut nidore altarium, vel hostiis pecudum saginati remissis, quae constrinxerant curasse videantur. Hi sunt et furentes, quos in publicum videtis excurrere; vates et ipsi absque templo sic insaniunt, sic bacchantur, sic rotantur. Par et in illis instigatio daemonis, sed :ARGUMENTUM dispar furoris. De ipsis etiam illa quae paulo ante tibi dicta sunt, ut Jupiter ludos repeteret ex somnio, ut cum equis Castores viderentur, ut cingulum matronae navicula sequeretur. Haec omnia sciunt plerique pars vestrum, ipsos daemonas de semetipsis confiteri, quoties a nobis et tormentis verborum et orationis incendiis de corporibus exiguntur. Ipse Saturnus, et Serapis, et Jupiter, et quidquid daemonum colitis, victi dolore, quod sunt eloquuntur: nec utique in turpitudinem sui, nonnullis praesertim vestrum assistentibus, mentiuntur. Ipsis testibus, esse eos daemonas, de se verum confitentibus credite. Adjurati enim per Deum verum et solum, inviti miseris corporibus inhorrescunt: et vel exsiliunt statim, vel evanescunt gradatim, prout fides patientis adjuvat, aut gratia curantis aspirat. Sic Christianos de proximo fugitant, quos longe in coetibus per vos lacessebant. Ideo inserti mentibus imperitorum, odium nostri serunt occulte per timorem: naturale est enim et odisse, quem timeas; et quem metueris, infestare, si possis. Sic occupant animos, et obstruunt pectora, ut ante nos incipiant homines odisse, quam nosse: ne cognitos aut imitari possint, aut damnare non possint.
pass_a_gloss: These impure spirits, demons, as shown by magicians, by philosophers, and by Plato, hide under statues and images consecrated, and by their breath gain authority, as if of a present divinity, while they inspire prophets, while they linger in temples, while they sometimes animate the fibers of entrails, govern the flights of birds, control lots, produce oracles wrapped in many falsehoods. For they both deceive and are deceived, so that they neither know sincere truth nor confess what they know to their own perdition. Thus they weigh down from heaven, and call away from the true God to material things, disturb life, disturb all, even secretly penetrating bodies, as thin spirits, they invent diseases, terrify minds, distort limbs, so that they may compel to their own worship: so that, fed on the smell of altars or on the sacrifices of animals, they may seem to have cured what they had bound. These are also the raving ones, whom you see rushing out in public; prophets also, without a temple, rave thus, become frenzied thus, spin around thus. Equal in them is the instigation of a demon, but different is the argument of frenzy. Also about them, those things which a little while ago were said to you, that Jupiter might repeat games from a dream, that Castors might seem to be seen with horses, that a matron's girdle might follow a little ship. All these things many of you know, that demons themselves confess about themselves, as often as they are driven out from bodies by our words and the fires of prayer. Saturn himself, and Serapis, and Jupiter, and whatever demons you worship, overcome by pain, speak out what they are: nor indeed do they lie, especially with some of you assisting, about their own shame. Believe them, themselves witnesses, that they are demons, confessing the truth about themselves. For when adjured by the true and only God, they shudder, unwilling, in wretched bodies: and either they leap out at once, or they gradually vanish, as the faith of the patient assists, or the grace of the healer inspires. Thus they flee from Christians, whom they had long been harassing in gatherings through you. Therefore, inserted in the minds of the unskilled, they secretly sow hatred of us through fear: for it is natural to hate him whom you fear, and to attack him whom you dread, if you can. Thus they occupy minds, and block hearts, so that men begin to hate us before they know us: lest they might be able to know or imitate, or not be able to condemn.

choices.english: lest they might be able to know or imitate, or not be able to condemn
rejected: lest, once they know us, they might be able to imitate us, or else find themselves unable to condemn us

pass_b_english: These impure spirits, these demons—as magicians, philosophers, and Plato himself have shown—hide beneath consecrated statues and images. By their breath they claim authority, as if a deity were truly present, while they inspire prophets, haunt temples, animate the fibers of entrails, direct the flight of birds, control the lots, and produce oracles wrapped in many falsehoods. For they both deceive and are deceived, so that they neither know sincere truth nor confess what they do know, to their own perdition.

Thus they weigh down from heaven and call men away from the true God to material things; they disturb life, they unsettle everyone, even secretly penetrating bodies like thin spirits. They invent diseases, terrify minds, distort limbs, all to compel worship of themselves—so that, fed by the smell of altars or the sacrifices of fattened beasts, they may seem to have cured the very ills they bound.

These are the raving ones you see rushing out in public; even prophets without a temple rave, frenzy, and spin in just this way. The demon's instigation in them is the same, but the argument of their frenzy differs. You also know the things I mentioned a little while ago: how Jupiter was made to renew games because of a dream, how the Castors seemed to appear with horses, how a matron's girdle followed a little ship. Many of you know all this, because the demons themselves confess it about themselves whenever they are driven from bodies by our words and the fires of prayer.

Saturn himself, Serapis, Jupiter, and whatever demons you worship—overcome by pain, they speak what they are. Nor do they lie about their own shame, especially with some of you standing by as witnesses. Believe them, since they themselves are witnesses confessing the truth about themselves. For when adjured by the true and only God, they shudder unwillingly in wretched bodies: they either leap out at once or fade away gradually, as the faith of the sufferer assists or the grace of the healer inspires.

Thus they flee from Christians at close range, whom they had long harassed in gatherings through you. Therefore, implanted in the minds of the ignorant, they secretly sow hatred of us through fear: for it is natural to hate him whom you fear, and to attack him whom you dread, if you can. Thus they occupy minds and block hearts, so that men begin to hate us before they know us—lest they be able to know or imitate, or be unable to condemn.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A preserves the nuances of the Latin clauses, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering without adding or contradicting the source. The translation of 'inserti mentibus imperitorum' as 'inserted in the minds of the unskilled' (Pass A) and 'implanted in the minds of the ignorant' (Pass B) correctly interprets 'imperitorum' in this context as a possible OCR/textual corruption or specific usage for those in command/unskilled, though the translation remains faithful to the provided Latin text. All clauses, including the complex final sentence, are accounted for.
